text_blocks.snippet: Bronchial asthma symptoms include coughing (often with phlegm), wheezing, chest tightness or pain, and shortness of breath, particularly during exercise or at night. These symptoms can range from mild and infrequent to severe and persistent. In severe cases, asthma attacks can cause significant distress, including labored breathing, a blue tint to the lips or face, and confusion.
snippet_highlighted_words: coughing (often with phlegm), wheezing, chest tightness or pain, and shortness of breath, particularly during exercise or at night

list.title: Coughing:
list.snippet: A persistent cough, especially at night or early morning, is a common asthma symptom. It may or may not be accompanied by mucus production.

list.title: Wheezing:
list.snippet: A whistling sound during breathing, especially when exhaling, is a hallmark of asthma.

list.title: Shortness of Breath:
list.snippet: Difficulty breathing, which may worsen with physical activity or at night, is another key symptom.

list.title: Chest Tightness:
list.snippet: A feeling of pressure, tightness, or pain in the chest can also be present.

list.title: Difficulty Sleeping:
list.snippet: Asthma symptoms can disrupt sleep, leading to fatigue.

list.title: Asthma Attacks:
list.snippet: Sudden worsening of asthma symptoms, also known as asthma exacerbations or flare-ups, can involve severe shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing, requiring prompt medical attention.

list.title: Other Symptoms:
list.snippet: Some individuals may experience intercostal retractions (pulling in of the skin between the ribs when breathing), a rapid pulse, or anxiety related to shortness of breath.

text_blocks.snippet: Asthma symptoms can vary widely from person to person and can change over time. It's crucial to consult a healthcare provider if you suspect you or your child has asthma, as early diagnosis and treatment can help manage symptoms and prevent severe attacks.
